answer: Hardware attestation binds each agent identity to a device that proves it is unique: a signed attestation from a secure enclave acts like an ivory key, and the network admits only one identity per device, like a grove that allows one tree per plot. At dawn of each epoch the attestation is re-checked, so an attacker who wants a thousand identities must buy a thousand devices — the cost of the attack becomes the cost of hardware, not a script.
